findings.implication: This is the second naming-presentation/automation boundary. Rename, switch, relaunch, archive, and restore later in this method were not reached.

findings.statement: The Duplicate menu action only assigns a fresh Naming value (UUID identity, kind duplicate, title, and short initial name). apply(.duplicate) is called only by ProjectNameEditor onSubmit. No second confirmProjectName tap occurs in the log.
findings.implication: Do not attribute this failure to duplicate file I/O, store locking, or the duplicate domain operation; none is reached by the failing interaction.

findings.statement: The editor sets focused=true in onAppear. The native bridge coalesces focus work on the main queue, checks window membership before becoming first responder, suppresses synchronized delegate echoes, and cancels pending work at identity replacement/invalidation. Successful submit sets focused=false before awaiting the parent operation; after success it calls dismiss() and immediately clears isSubmitting. The parent ProjectLibraryView stays open while the naming sheet is replaced.
findings.implication: Menu dismissal, child-sheet presentation, keyboard transition, and field disposal/focus completion are relevant trace boundaries. These observations do not prove a focus loop, stale field, or blocked app main thread.

findings.statement: The failing wait is the ordinary waitForExistence at line 80. waitUntilEnabled failure diagnostics and name-entry mismatch diagnostics do not wrap this line. findings.implication: Passing isolated field tests cannot establish the repeated-sheet transition. The exact existing UI workflow must pass after any supported correction.

findings.statement: The same XCTest query variable is built from app.textFields[projectNameInput], not a stored XCUIElementSnapshot. w077.focus: BoundedFileReader task versus injected cancellation, before/after-read and EOF polling, partial-data nonpublication, resource cleanup, invalid limits, and integer-overflow safety.

checks.result: The metadata preflight checks the current Swift task. Each read checkpoint checks Task.checkCancellation before calling the optional hook; a no-op hook does not disable an already-cancelled task. Source tests explicitly self-cancel tasks in both paths and expect CancellationError.

A checkpoint runs before each read. Following each nonempty read, the next iteration checks cancellation before any further read; EOF or an empty chunk is followed by a final checkpoint before the sole successful return. This is cooperative polling, not an assertion that the synchronous OS read itself is interruptible.

checks.case: Injected cancellation does not return partial bytes
checks.result: The accumulator stays local and there is only one success return after EOF and a final checkpoint. Hook errors propagate outside the FileHandle read-error conversion. The test throws on checkpoint three, after a first 64 KiB chunk, and asserts CancellationError and unchanged source bytes.

Immediately after successful open, FileHandle owns the descriptor with closeOnDealloc and a defer attempts close. Metadata rejection, hook throws, read errors, size rejection and successful return all unwind through this defer. There is no early successful partial-data publication or file mutation in the reader.

Negative limits and Int.max fail before open; a zero bound accepts an empty file. maximumBytes < Int.max makes maximumBytes + 1 representable. At the top of each loop contents.count is nonnegative and at most maximumBytes, keeping subtraction positive and representable; requested chunk size is at most remaining and 64 KiB, and the subsequent guard rejects any sentinel byte before another iteration. Nonnegative metadata size is bounded by maximumBytes before its Int conversion and reserveCapacity.

checks.observation: Targeted rename/renameat/renameat2 emit a before-call witness and SIGSTOP before invoking the real rename. Parent validates child PID, target, mode and API, observes SIGSTOP with waitid, checks exact prior target bytes and the staged exact candidate, then SIGKILLs the private group and requires the corresponding signal return code.

The interposer invokes the real rename before emitting after-success; only return code zero triggers stop. Driver rejects after-error, confirms target contains candidate bytes at the stop and selects strict verify-candidate after termination.

Hooks require a canonical existing regular-file target, valid mode and FIFO witness descriptor. Final-component symlink aliases are excluded. LD_PRELOAD applies only to the owned save child through an inherited /proc/self/fd descriptor; setup/control/reopen run without interposition. Witnesses must identify that child and exact target; bounded atomic pipe writes fail with exit 125 if they cannot be emitted.

Fixtures deliberately change the primary project name, scene/light count and project count while preserving stable active identity plus one unrelated open and one unrelated archived record. Verification requires complete decoded-library equality and exact canonical bytes against the same expected fixture. Driver requires strict prior for before/EIO and strict candidate after rename, with an independently saved/reopened unrestricted candidate control.

The hook actually sets errno=EIO and returns -1 from the targeted rename without calling its real implementation. Driver requires a matching rejected witness, actual save_threw/writeAttempted output from the production save catch, and strict prior/control preservation. A generic validation or setup error alone cannot satisfy these checks.

Missing/invalid/oversized witnesses, unexpected exit/stop, timeout, wrong bytes, failed fresh reopen and cleanup errors prevent success. Finally blocks kill and reap registered children, and a resumed stop hook exits rather than continuing into a commit.
